answer: With 500 abstracts per domain under condition C, both rank-frequency curves remain Zipf-like: k = 1.125 (R² 0.961) for GLP-1 (medical) and k = 1.073 (R² 0.962) for Machine learning (computing), a difference of 0.051. The overall shape is therefore similar, but the details are domain-specific. GLP-1 (medical) has 12,626 distinct terms versus 15,191 for Machine learning (computing) (49.7% vs 50.9% hapax), and only 22.4% of the combined vocabulary is shared. The top-10 lists share 0 terms (none); the other head terms name each domain's subject (glp-1, receptor, patients, weight, metabolic, obesity, risk, agonists, diabetes, outcomes vs model, learning, using, performance, models, study, analysis, data, clinical, machine). Domain specificity thus changes which terms occupy the head and how large the tail is, while the heavy-tailed form persists. Two single-topic samples cannot establish a general effect size; the exponent also depends on preprocessing and the fitted rank range.
